slot.subtopic: Stability of alkenes / heat of hydrogenation
slot.brief: Give four isomeric alkenes (with cis/trans and substitution variation) and rank by heat of hydrogenation; students must translate stability ordering into ΔH values.

stem: For hydrogenation to the corresponding alkanes, arrange these alkenes by signed $\Delta H_{\mathrm{hyd}}$, from most negative to least negative.

verdicts.working: Hydrogenation is most exothermic for the least stable alkene. Stability increases as pent-1-ene < cis-pent-2-ene < trans-pent-2-ene < 2-methylbut-2-ene, so the signed hydrogenation enthalpies follow the same order from most negative to least negative.

working:
Alkene stability: trisubstituted $>$ trans-disubstituted $>$ cis-disubstituted $>$ monosubstituted. Greater stability gives less exothermic hydrogenation; hence $\Delta H_{\mathrm{hyd}}$: pent-1-ene $<$ cis-pent-2-ene $<$ trans-pent-2-ene $<$ 2-methylbut-2-ene.

Independent check: Hydrogenation is most exothermic for the least stable alkene. Stability increases as pent-1-ene < cis-pent-2-ene < trans-pent-2-ene < 2-methylbut-2-ene, so the signed hydrogenation enthalpies follow the same order from most negative to least negative.
solution: Alkene stability increases in the order $\text{pent-1-ene} < \text{cis-pent-2-ene} < \text{trans-pent-2-ene} < \text{2-methylbut-2-ene}$. More stable alkenes have less exothermic hydrogenation, so $\Delta H_{\mathrm{hyd}}$ follows this same order from most negative to least negative.
